timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: I keep hearing about the OSI model but never understood why it matters for security.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: It's a map of every layer where attacks can happen. Miss one layer and you're vulnerable there.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Exactly. Cables, connectors, physical taps. An attacker can literally clip onto a wire and read everything.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: That's primitive. Most attacks are online, right?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Layer 7 gets all the headlines, but Layer 2 ARP spoofing redirects traffic without touching your firewall.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: So a firewall doesn't protect against Layer 2 attacks?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: No. Firewalls operate at Layers 3-7. Layer 2 is below them. That's why switch security matters.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Layer 4 is TCP hijacking. Layer 5 manages sessions. Layer 6 handles encryption. Each has its own attack surface.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: This is overwhelming. How do you secure all seven layers?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: You don't secure all seven equally. You identify which layers your traffic uses and secure every one of those.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: That actually makes sense. Defense in depth across all layers.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Now you're thinking like a security architect.
